model: proportional-odds (cumulative logit) regression: P(level <= k) = sigmoid(theta_k - sum_j weight_j * clip((x_j - mean_j) / sd_j, -z_clip, z_clip)); a missing x_j takes the training median.

caveat: An estimate of the CEFR level of a reading text (material written or chosen for learners), learned from Cambridge exam passages and ELG-CEFR-EN graded texts. It describes the text, not a writer's proficiency: do not use it to grade learner writing, where it does no better than always answering B2. Not applicable under 100 words.

summary_for_users.text: Tested on 706 exam and graded reading passages it hadn't seen (5-fold cross-validation), the estimate was within one level of the published level 92% of the time and exactly right 52% of the time; the shown range contained the published level 88% of the time. Trained on one collection and tested on the other, within-one accuracy was 83% at worst. It is for reading texts, not for grading writing.

evaluation.choice_rule: The sign-constrained feature set with the higher cross-validated QWK on texts of 100+ words (sign constraints fixed in advance, for readable contributions). Only sets computable from run_all's results were eligible; the CVLA-index sets need the parsed Analysis and are reported for comparison.

decision.rule: Don't ship if cross-validated within-one accuracy is below 85% or either leave-one-dataset-out within-one accuracy is below 80% (texts of 100+ words).

baselines_on_training_texts_100_plus_wor.note: estimated_level_95th is not fitted to these texts, so its figures are out-of-sample; compare it with the leave-one-dataset-out figures as well as CV.

ace_cefr.note: Only a handful of Ace-CEFR passages reach 50 words, and none reaches the 100-word floor, so the shipped estimator would answer none of them; the figures are the raw model, for completeness only.

icle500.what: ICLE learner essays (graded at the writer's level)

cvla_published.what: CVLA Reading mode as published (Uchida & Negishi 2018, sec. 3.5): mean of four per-index regressions on ARI, verbs per sentence, mean CEFR-J level of content words, and B/A content-word ratio; CEFR-J level from the published bands, folded to six levels (Pre-A1 and A1.x = A1, ..., B2.x = B2, C1 < 5, C2 >= 5). Computed with lexinspect's spaCy tags and CEFR-J 1.5 (the paper used TreeTagger and CEFR-J 1.3). Calibrated on A1-B2 coursebooks, so C1/C2 are extrapolation.

ensemble_ordinal_plus_cvla.what: round((expected level under study5_24_signed + CVLA level) / 2)

evaluation.method: Stratified 5-fold CV (seed 0) on the pooled reading texts; within each training fold the L2 penalty is chosen from [0.3, 1.0, 3.0, 10.0, 30.0, 100.0] by inner 3-fold CV on QWK, and the imputation medians, means and SDs are fitted on the training fold only. Leave-one-dataset-out fits on one collection and tests on the other; a model fitted on one collection can only predict the levels it saw. 'applicable' = texts of 100+ lexinspect words, the floor below which the estimator declines. range_80 is the shortest run of adjacent levels holding 80% of the probability. Length is lexinspect's readability word count.

metadata.licence_note: The coefficients, thresholds and standardisation figures in this file are derived from datasets licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Xia, Kochmar & Briscoe 2016; Breuker 2023; both via UniversalCEFR), and the Cambridge readability data's own terms limit information derived from it to non-commercial research and education. This file is therefore treated as an adaptation and licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No text from the datasets is included. The estimate is offered in free, non-commercial lexinspect; the MIT licence of lexinspect's code does not extend to this file.
metadata.open_alternative_checked: No openly licensed (CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0) CEFR-labelled set of reading passages of comparable size was found: OneStopEnglish (CC BY-SA 4.0) has three non-CEFR levels; Ace-CEFR (CC0) is short conversational text (median 10 words); CLEAR is CC BY-NC-SA and US-grade based.
